summary: A per-feature GAME gate for world-engine features, so a feature can go on being developed in the lab while drawing nothing in the game until it is ready. Generalises the ONE-entry GATE_RULINGS map (drivers/index.js:475) that F35's TERMINATOR_ENABLED already established, on the same 'one declared value, read by every producer' pattern. Max's bar, ruled 2026-09-04: ON only if the feature reads the bake's accumulated landforms, not just the province mask.

ruling.bar: Grown from the engine, not painted on.
ruling.informedOf: that it removes most of the landform detail he accepted the session before, and the game will look barer until each feature is developed
rejected: off = anything whose LOOK he has not passed (would also take the rivers)
off = only the provably dead (F43 facets, F46 mats)

theList.measuredIn: src/worldengine/shaders/height.glsl.js, verified per combiner rather than taken from prose

OFF_painted_over.why: read neither the accumulated height nor its gradient — they synthesise their own noise and amplitude-modulate it by the 3-channel province mask, with floors of 0.15-0.50 so they still render where the mask says they do not belong
OFF_painted_over.waitingFor: any of the three jobs in solid-relief-deck/FOLLOWUP-not-fully-developed.md; (b) — make the combiner read the accumulated relief — is the one that clears this bar

STAY_ON_reactive.why: mass-wasting reads the host-slope RESIDUAL gradIn - gradBase (height.glsl.js:1364), which is zero on flat ground, so the combiner returns before writing. It is the only one of the eleven whose terrain read CLOSES as relief goes to zero.

ALREADY_DEAD.why: their inputs are identically zero, so they render nothing today; they get a gate row for honesty rather than a behaviour change

NOT_IN_SCOPE_OF_THE_BAR.why: the bar is about landform features painted over the relief bake. Atmosphere, optics, aurora, storms and rings are driven straight off the condition vector, which IS the engine's own output — 'reads the accumulated relief' is not a meaningful test for them. They keep their current state and get a gate row recording that.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The features that are just painted over the world engine draw nothing in the game.

verifyVia.input: Headless: resolve the driver packs over the corpus with the gates applied.
verifyVia.observable: Each of the eight OFF features publishes its master gate as 0 on every body (baseline: they publish live values on 10-103 bodies each). The three reactive ones and every non-relief feature are unchanged.

verification.how: tests/world-engine-feature-gates.test.js over the 124-body solid corpus: each of the eight OFF masters reaches 0 bodies (was 103/124/122/124/46/103/40/68); the three reactive ones are unmoved by value. Resolved through the same writer the game runs, not read off a flag.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The switch actually controls the render — it is not a flag that reads itself back.

verifyVia.input: SABOTAGE, both directions, on a body where the feature is live: force one gate OFF and measure the rendered contribution; force it back ON and measure again.
verifyVia.observable: OFF removes the feature's pixels and ON restores them, on the same body and the same frame budget. A gate that cannot be shown to bite FAILS this AC — reading the constant back does not count.

verification.verdict: PASS (headless, with a discriminating control) — the live half NOT captured
verification.how: The gate is proven to bite: RULED must DIFFER from ALL_ON on every OFF row and go all the way to zero, and AC-5 flips one back to its full count. ⛔ The FIRST cut of this instrument was VACUOUS and is the reason the control is shaped that way: it fed ray-pack-corpus's already-resolved numbers back into resolveDriver, so the gate branch never saw a descriptor, and it reported mountains:103 with the gate OFF while its own liveness check passed. Fixed by taking descriptors from solidReliefPack. ⚠ NOT closed in the browser: repeated attempts to read the mounted game material's relief uniforms via bodySurfaces/previewPack returned nothing usable, so 'the pixels are gone on a live body' is asserted headlessly, not seen.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: I can carry on developing those features in the lab exactly as before.

verifyVia.input: Load the lab and drive the same features.
verifyVia.observable: Every feature still renders and still responds to its lab control; the lab's own per-feature *Enabled state is untouched. The gate is GAME-side only — asserted, because this is the one divergence the workstream deliberately creates.

verification.how: In the running lab, hard-reloaded: with the lab's own feature checkboxes on (_lab.enableAllFeatures), every game-gated feature is alive on Mars — uMountainAmp 0.4775, uChasmaDepth 0.0362, uScarpStrength 0.0762, uPlateauStrength 0.0258, uLavaCoverage 0.15, uSubStrength 0.0222. gatesFor's default map answers all eleven true for the lab while the game's map answers eight false, read in-page. ⭐ This is the claim the workstream exists for and it is the one verified live.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: There is one place that tells me, per feature, whether it is on in the game and what it is waiting for — and it lives with the world engine.

verifyVia.input: Read the registry module and the F-spine table.
verifyVia.observable: Every gated feature has a row carrying its state, the reason, and its named exit condition. A test asserts the registry and the F-spine table cannot disagree, and that no gated feature is missing a row — so the documentation cannot rot silently.

verification.how: SOLID_RELIEF_GAME_GATES carries state + reason + exit per row; the rulings map is DERIVED from it, never restated. Tests fail if a gate has no row, if an OFF row names no exit, or if an ON row is still waiting for something. Prose home: the PLAN's THE GAME GATES section.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When a feature is ready, switching it on in the game is one change, not a re-wiring job.

verifyVia.input: Flip one feature's declared value and re-resolve the packs.
verifyVia.observable: That feature's master gate returns to its live per-body values with no other edit anywhere. Demonstrated in a test that flips a gate and asserts the values come back.

verification.how: Flipping `mountains` alone returns it to all 103 bodies with no other edit, and disturbs no other row.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Flying around, the game still looks coherent — barer, but nothing broken or half-drawn.

verifyVia.input: Max flies the live build and looks at several solid worlds.
verifyVia.observable: Holistic: the worlds read as simpler rather than damaged — no missing-texture look, no features half-present, no world that now reads as a bare sphere when it should not.

verification.how: UAT. No agent closes this — and it is the one that matters here, because the game is deliberately barer.

inputs: src/worldengine/drivers/index.js:475 GATE_RULINGS — the existing one-entry registry this generalises; its own docblock says 'ONE ENTRY TODAY' and describes the three-producer pattern
src/worldengine/drivers/solidOptics.js:247 TERMINATOR_ENABLED — the precedent: one declared constant beside the pack that emits the uniform, carrying Max's words on the line
src/worldengine/drivers/solidRelief.js — the eleven master gates the bar applies to
src/worldengine/shaders/height.glsl.js — where 'reads the accumulated surface' was measured per combiner
docs/FEATURES/one-pipeline-two-frontends-PLAN.md — the F-row spine table, the documentation home
outputs: a game-side gate registry module, one declared value per feature, with its reason and exit condition
the pack writer that zeroes an OFF feature's master gate (the shape TERMINATOR_ENABLED already uses)
the F-spine table rows, which gain the game-gate state
mustStayWorking: THE LAB. It keeps every feature on — that is where development continues, and it is the whole point. This is the one deliberate lab/game divergence in the codebase with a sanctioned exit; per converge-dont-declare-divergence every OFF row is DEBT with a named condition, never a steady state.
The three reactive features (karst, dunes, mass-wasting) and every non-relief feature must be untouched — verified by value, not by inspection.
The shared RNG draw stream — the gate is a read-time multiply, it must not touch generation. Instrument B's DRAW STREAM channel must stay green.

Pack contract shape — the packs still publish every uniform they publish today; an OFF feature publishes its gate as 0, it does not stop publishing the name (a vanishing uniform would break the pack-contract tests and the lab's read-back).
The lab's own read-back of the packs (world-engine-lab.html imports several pack modules) must not start seeing zeroed game gates.

foundWhileBuilding: The gate mechanism ALREADY EXISTED and had never been used: solidRelief declared all eleven gate names, gatesFor answered GATE_RULINGS[g] ?? true, and index.js:267's own comment said 'all eleven default ON and none is ruled off today'. The work was the RULING plus splitting the two kinds of ruling apart — not building a switch.

GATE_RULINGS was read by BOTH front-ends through one shared runPacks, so the first cut silenced the lab. Caught by material-parity-list as eight names leaving LEDGER.labVarying. Fixed by giving each sink its own rulings map.

The game's own preview provenance string (main.js:4071) was printing GATE_RULINGS — after the split that is the LAB's map, so the preview would have quietly described the wrong front-end. Re-pointed to GAME_GATE_RULINGS.

uatCorrection.max: Everything still has the dunes drawn across the surface. Otherwise seems about right. (2026-09-04)
uatCorrection.whatItFound: The bar as first applied admitted dunes and karst because they 'read the accumulated surface'. But their gates (lowGround, gentle) are smoothsteps DOWN from relief: turning the other eight off FLATTENED the field they read, both terms went to 1, and only the province floor (0.30 / 0.25) remained. The first cut made dunes WORSE, by its own doing.
uatCorrection.theSharpenedBar: Reacting to relief is not the same as reacting to its absence. PERMISSIVE gates (lowGround/gentle) open on flat ground; RESIDUAL gates (gradIn - gradBase) close. Only the latter survives its neighbours being switched off.
uatCorrection.karst: NOT named by Max. Ruled off on the character-identical gate rather than waiting for the next UAT to find it; one flip returns it.

shipped.uat: Max 2026-09-04: "Otherwise seems about right" — accepted with the dune defect named, which this commit fixes.
